facts.text: Standing Rock gets its name from a sandstone boulder erected by Creek Indians around 1836, just before their forced removal on the Trail of Tears.
A post office opened in Standing Rock in 1837 and operated intermittently until 1986, serving as a key hub for mail and local commerce.
The community was founded in the 1830s, shortly after Chambers County was formed in 1832 from Creek lands ceded by treaty.
Early settlers cleared land for cotton along Wehadkee Creek, attracting migrants from Georgia and other eastern states to build plantations in the 1840s.
The Standing Rock Methodist Church traces its roots to 1835, evolving from the Conway Mill Society that first met in a log schoolhouse.
In 1935, the Rural Electrification Administration extended electricity to Standing Rock, modernizing farms and homes in the Piedmont region.
